modification_assessment.assessment_basis: Static ASUS package and payload bytes, exact-revision public definitions, current public Linux driver source, and the ASUS vendor release note. No physical ASUS card, behavior, authentication path, or hardware result is established.

asus_gfx_info.reason: The checked Linux header defines GFX_INFO v3.0, not v3.1, and the driver union/parser handles v2.2, v2.4, v2.7, and v3.0. No v3.1 CU count or mask is inferred.

cu_stream_processor_audit.editing_go_no_go: NO-GO: no ASUS CU unlock field or candidate image is established; editing cannot restore fused-off or physically absent resources.
cu_stream_processor_audit.investigation_go_no_go: GO: continue static source tracing and, only after exact ASUS card identification, compare read-only runtime CU topology with hardware/ASIC evidence.
cu_stream_processor_audit.other_asus_tables: umc_info v4.0 reports memory metadata only; no CU or stream-processor field is defined in the matching structure. No other decoded ASUS table exposes an active-CU mask.
cu_stream_processor_audit.policy_vs_hardware: The public gfx_info v3.0 definition includes maximum topology/configuration fields such as max_cu_per_sh, which are not by themselves proof of enabled units. Actual available resources require exact-card driver/runtime topology plus silicon fuse/harvest state; physically absent resources cannot be supplied by a VBIOS policy change.
cu_stream_processor_audit.public_definition: The checked Linux atomfirmware.h contains atom_gfx_info_v3_0 but no v3.1 definition. The public amdgpu driver union includes v2.2, v2.4, v2.7 and v3.0; its get_gfx_info path accepts v3.0 content 0 and v2.4/v2.7, so this observed v3.1 table exposes no safely decoded CU count or mask in this analysis.
cu_stream_processor_audit.xfx_context_boundary: The repository's 64-active-CU observation is for an XFX-subsystem device only. It is not used to infer ASUS hardware capability.

scope: Static analysis of the ASUS package and its two extracted ROM payloads, with an optional bounded XFX software-ROM comparison. No updater, firmware, or hardware was executed or modified.

analysis_tools.limits: GNU file, objdump, and strings are used as static format/section/string probes. readelf is ELF-only and is not used to claim successful PE parsing.

tianocompress.build_command: make -C BaseTools/Source/C/Common -f GNUmakefile -j2; make -C BaseTools/Source/C/TianoCompress -f GNUmakefile -j2

tianocompress.rebuild_identity_note: This executable was rebuilt from the pinned EDK II source commit. The earlier recorded binary was absent, so byte-for-byte restoration cannot be asserted; the decompressed GOP output hash was reproduced.

references.scope: PCI option-ROM image boundaries, EFI image header, code types, and alignment.
UEFI compression type 1 envelope, compressed/original sizes, and zero terminator.

references.scope: Exact public ATOM structures and revision-specific field names used by this analyzer. No GFX 3.1 or SMC/DPM 6.0 body definition is present at this commit.
Cross-checks legacy table names and the known indirect-I/O structure. Its body layout is not applied where the ASUS record's observed revision or declared size does not match.

references.scope: Driver-side revision handling for GFX, FirmwareInfo, and UMC ECC metadata; this is source interpretation, not proof of ASUS runtime behavior.

channel_width.source_note: Current upstream amdgpu_atomfirmware_get_umc_info() explicitly accepts ATOM UMC format/content revision 4.0, reads v40.channel_num and v40.channel_width, and computes vram_width = channel_num * (1 << channel_width). areas.area: Core clocks, voltage, power and efficiency

local_evidence.notes: Boot clock/voltage slots reserved; PowerPlayInfo master pointer null; MACO/USB mode-specific limits are zero, not general board power limits.

The nonzero ID differs from ASUS 0x00001296. Current upstream SMU14 carries the ID into setup and can select a matching entry from a v2.1 directory in driver SMC firmware; the exact blobs and selected entries for these images are not present here, and exact R9700 runtime dispatch is unverified.
No exact public structure definition found; older layouts not applied.
Different from ASUS in six bytes; does not decode ASUS body.

areas.likely_control_layer: Driver/SMU PowerPlay policy, PMFW combo-table policy on the conditional SMU 14.0.2/14.0.3 path, and board power delivery; the exact R9700/ASUS MP1 dispatch remains unknown.
runtime_leads: AMD SMI documents runtime power-cap, clock-level/limit, performance-level, overdrive and telemetry APIs where supported; exact SKU and driver support was not exercised here.

The host records failed overdrive-table uploads during resume. An external R9700 report attributes similar errors to writes during runtime-PM resume and warns that sysfs requested-value readback may remain visible after failed upload; this is unverified third-party evidence and not a diagnosis of this host.

AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 ROCm/PyTorch guide Rev. 2.0 describes a compute-optimized runtime profile favoring sustained clocks and higher power limits. Current Linux ppfeaturemask is a separate driver-side gate; its PP_OVERDRIVE_MASK value 0x4000 is not the ATOM FirmwareInfo bit 0x00004000, whose meaning remains unknown. No guide commands were run and exact R9700 support is not established.

An external R9700 OC/UV report updated through 2026-08-04 records Linux 7.0.0-28 / ROCm 7.14 / amdgpu DKMS 6.19.4 sample results: an OD_MCLK request of 1350 MHz read back while DPM remained topped at 1258 MHz; after cooler service, one card measured about 295 W instead of about 222 W; the report also says a 330 W cap that previously failed above 300 W later applied after service, with 393 W peak and about 320 W average, but the author cannot tell whether firmware or hardware changed, and a -120 mV run reported +7.7% sustained prefill at nearly equal power, whereas -150 mV plus 330 W crashed a deeper run. A separate personal report describes workload-specific 210 W savings but errors/hangs at -100 mV. These are non-ASUS reports with conflicting sample/workload outcomes, not safe values or VBIOS evidence.

Current upstream amdgpu_drv.c documents smu_pptable_id (-1 automatic, 0 VBIOS, positive driver soft-pptable ID); SMU14 setup honors the override. A separate table-microcode path is gated by PSP firmware loading, SCPM, non-SR-IOV state and IP version. This is a driver policy source-selection lead, not a VBIOS field; no selector was changed and exact R9700 applicability/ID availability are unknown.

Current upstream amdgpu_drv.c initializes ppfeaturemask to generic default 0xfff7bfff and comments OverDrive (bit 14) and GFX DCS (bit 19) disabled by default. The amd_shared.h enum assigns 0x4000 to PP_OVERDRIVE_MASK. This is driver runtime policy, distinct from the ATOM FirmwareInfo bit 0x00004000, which remains unknown; the generic mask is not an R9700-specific setting recommendation.

Current upstream dispatches MP1 IP 14.0.2/14.0.3 to smu_v14_0_2. That implementation obtains a combo PowerPlay table from PMFW, gates OverDrive using FeatureCtrlMask, and derives fan availability from the PMFW table. This setup path does not use generic smu_v14_0_setup_pptable PPLib-ID selection; the exact ASUS R9700 IP version/path is not established, so the two paths remain conditional alternatives.

Current upstream SMU 14.0.2 expects driver interface 0x2e, while external R9700 issue logs report PMFW 0x32 or 0x33. User reports of fan/gpu_od failures conflict with AMD-contributor reports that mismatch is usually nonfatal and gpu_od exists on their R9700. A community patch changes the expected interface to 0x33 and claims fan/BACO/idle-power improvements; it is not upstream validation and warns that metrics compatibility needs checking.

An AMD contributor reported reproducing an R9700 s2idle SMU/DPM resume failure and submitting an amdgpu patch; the issue remained open without a linked patch on 2026-10-19. The migrated TheRock #9228 (formerly legacy #6347, same issue) describes process-start-dependent throughput: slow and fast states show similar SCLK, forcing high DPM did not prevent transitions, manually pinning highest DPM reduced boost, and later comments report the split with some graph/attention configurations but not another tested configuration. Authors suspect process/queue or capture initialization but identify no cause. These remain software/runtime evidence leads, not VBIOS behavior.

Current upstream SMU 14.0.2 declares runtime OverDrive controls for GFX V/F points, UCLK min/max, fan-curve temperature/PWM points, minimum PWM, target temperature, acoustic thresholds, and zero-RPM settings. Linux documents these fan controls as staged settings that require a c commit. An external R9700 tuning report says readback can show staged values while the fan still uses the previous curve until commit. This is a generic driver/PMFW control path; exact ASUS R9700 dispatch and gpu_od availability are unverified, so it is a runtime alternative to investigate rather than a VBIOS field.

A Reddit ASUS Turbo owner report says the AS07 ROM reduced minimum fan speed from 30% to 12%, and another user says a full power cycle was needed. The linked thread names 7551OG.23.8.0.68.AS07.rom, but supplies no raw hash, measurement log, or byte-to-field mapping. This is a user-reported stock firmware outcome, not verified against the local unassociated AS07 payload.

ROCm issue #5908 reports PMFW 104.75/interface 0x32 plus an SMU previous-command timeout and GFX ring timeout alongside input-lag/PCIe symptoms. It is an external runtime report and does not establish that the interface mismatch caused those symptoms.

An Aug 2026 update to ROCm issue #6101 reports three R9700s across ASUS and ASRock boards with PMFW 104.76/interface 0x33; fan response reportedly degraded while runtime PM was disabled and the SMU later hung. This weakens a simple runtime-suspend explanation but does not establish the interface or VBIOS as cause.

ROCm TheRock issue #9245 reports roughly 3-4% GFX activity and 18-19 W per card for three R9700s with an idle HIP model, versus 0% and 12-13 W using an equivalent Vulkan server. This is an external backend/runtime efficiency comparison, not a VBIOS result.

ROCm/TheRock issue #9299 reports SMU message timeouts and MES queue failures ending in full host hangs on two dual-R9700 setups. One report logs PMFW 104.79/interface 0x33 and MP1 14.0.0, normal temperatures and a 230 W cap; its author correlates events with bursty clock/power changes alongside SDMA/PCIe traffic. A second contributor reports a similar failure with another R9700 firmware string. Current upstream dispatch maps MP1 14.0.0 to smu_v14_0_0, separate from the 14.0.2/14.0.3 path; neither path is established for the unassociated ASUS images. These external reports do not prove a VBIOS fault or field.

An Aug 2026 update to ROCm issue #6101 reports two ASUS boards with VBIOS part 115-G287BP00-100 whose fan response reportedly reversed in a later run: about 2,350-2,520 RPM at 99-101 C junction versus about 3,500 RPM near 65 C, with a roughly 303 W sample. Runtime PM was held active; one card later stopped answering SMU requests. The local AS04/AS07 bytes contain the same part label, but the report gives no ROM hash or AS04/AS07 version, so it cannot be tied to either payload. This is a runtime/SMU diagnostic lead, not proof of a VBIOS fan-table cause.

Current upstream dispatch sends MP1 14.0.0 to the separate smu_v14_0_0 path. That generic implementation marks itself APU-oriented and uses driver interface 0x7; the shared SMU 14.0 header lists 0x2e for the 14.0.2 path. In the 14.0.0 sensor code, VDDGFX and VDDSOC metric cases return zero. External issue #9299 reports an R9700 with MP1 14.0.0 and PMFW interface 0x33, but does not establish that current upstream generic code or its telemetry path matches the R9700 driver/firmware pair. This is a source-matching/measurement-quality lead, not a ROM field.

AMD SMI 27.2.0 official install/CLI docs state that AMD SMI gets metrics through amdgpu and version mismatches can make fields unavailable or N/A, including unsupported gpu_metrics layouts. Any R9700 clock/power/voltage observation needs the driver and AMD SMI versions recorded and compatible; no query was run.

AMD SMI 27.1.0 Python API documents read-only power/voltage and clock/VF observations: amdsmi_get_power_info returns power, power limit and GFX/SOC/memory voltages where exposed; amdsmi_get_gpu_metrics_info reports current clocks/voltages/power metrics where the layout supports them; amdsmi_get_clk_freq returns supported frequencies and current index; amdsmi_get_gpu_od_volt_info returns V/F curve points and SCLK/MCLK ranges, with num_regions=0 meaning unsupported. Several calls are unsupported in VM guests. Exact R9700 exposure is unverified and metrics can be unavailable/N/A across driver/library layout mismatches; no query was run.

AMD SMI 27.1.0 C/C++ reference also documents bare-metal Linux setters for SCLK/MCLK ranges and voltage/frequency curve points (amdsmi_set_gpu_od_clk_info and amdsmi_set_gpu_od_volt_info); VM guests are unsupported. This is a runtime control/characterization path, not a persistent VBIOS edit, and exact R9700 support was not checked or exercised.
areas.custom_vbios_relevance: No editable general clock/voltage/power field is decoded. ASUS officially says AS07 refines the fan curve, and one user reports a 30%-to-12% minimum-fan change after a full power cycle, but no altered byte is mapped and the local payload is unassociated. Generic SMU/AMDGPU exposes runtime fan and V/F controls on some paths; exact ASUS R9700 interface availability is unresolved. Trace the exact active driver/SMU/PMFW policy before considering persistence; SMC/DPM v6.0 remains opaque.
areas.confidence: High for local bytes, exact FirmwareInfo fields and public source behavior; low for ASUS runtime consequences.
unknowns: Exact-card SMU feature support and driver table selection

local_evidence.artifact: AS04, AS07, and XFX software ROM
local_evidence.notes: UMC record has no memory timing or voltage table; VRAMInfo pointer is null. Current upstream amdgpu_atomfirmware_get_umc_info() accepts UMC format/content revision 4.0 and computes width as channel_num * (1 << channel_width), giving 16 * 16 = 256 bits here. This is source-code interpretation, not a package measurement.
Kernel logs MEM ECC is active, GECC disabled, SRAM ECC not presented; no error-injection or workload correction test. AMD SMI reports Samsung GDDR6, a tool-reported field rather than package marking.
Current public ATOM headers define GDDR6 timing/init and voltage-object structures under other revisions, but no table is present at these pointers. Do not apply those layouts to the ASUS payload.

areas.likely_control_layer: DRAM population and board routing; UMC/SMU/PMFW policy; PSP/driver memory-training path; voltage rails and silicon support.
external_leads: A third-party two-Gigabyte-card report describes differing memory vendor/VBIOS samples and different memory-overdrive outcomes, then revises its initial silicon explanation after service corrected a thermal-interface issue. No ROM hashes or exact memory-table decode; unverified.

AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 ROCm/PyTorch guide Rev. 2.0 documents GPU internal-memory bandwidth diagnostics as a characterization path; it does not define memory timings or voltage, and the diagnostic was not run.

An external R9700 tuning report updated through 2026-08-04 describes a Samsung sample where OD_MCLK 1300/1350 MHz readback did not raise the 1258 MHz DPM top; sampled load clocks topped at 875 MHz, and a separate 1329 MHz setting correlated with a 1124 MHz maximum and 6.6% lower decode throughput. A companion two-card report describes 1349 MHz as no gain on an Hynix sample but about 20% lower decode on a Samsung sample as MCLK fell to roughly 772-875 MHz. These detailed user reports are specific to other boards/workloads and driver stacks; they do not identify ASUS timing fields or establish a firmware cause.

Current Linux ATOM headers define GDDR6 AC timing, memory-module and UMC-init structures under separate vram_info revisions, including v2.5; ASUS vram_info is null, so these structures are not decoded or transferred.
The generic SMU 14.0.2 feature map names VMEMP_SCALING and VDDIO_MEM_SCALING, but this does not prove those features are enabled or available on a particular R9700 and supplies no voltage values.

Upstream AMDGPU documents forcelongtraining as forcing long memory training on resume (default zero selects short training). PSP code separately reads a runtime-database two-stage DRAM-training bit and has cold-boot/resume training calls. These driver/PSP controls may be relevant to resume diagnosis, but exact ASUS R9700 execution is unknown. ASUS FirmwareInfo capability 0x00024000 leaves ENABLE_2STAGE_BIST_TRAINING (0x400) clear; that is not evidence that all memory training is disabled.
areas.custom_vbios_relevance: No timing or voltage target. ECC-capable metadata and default-enable state are separate. The public GDDR6 timing schemas are under other vram_info revisions, while the ASUS vram_info and voltageobject_info pointers are null. Generic SMU memory-voltage names and PSP training paths do not identify ASUS values. A PSP GECC boot-configuration path exists; changing VBIOS flags is not shown to enable correction. AMD SMI setter APIs provide a separate runtime clock/voltage control path where supported, but they expose no DRAM timing values and do not establish a persistent VBIOS target.
areas.confidence: High for UMC bytes and Linux parser distinction; low for physical DRAM, timing margins, voltage headroom and live ECC correction.

read_only_queries: amdsmi_get_gpu_ras_block_features_enabled: per-RAS-block status, a separate observation from ECC state
amdsmi_get_gpu_mem_overdrive_level: runtime memory-clock overdrive percent, not DRAM timing values
amdsmi_get_clk_freq: supported clock frequencies and current index for a requested domain
amdsmi_get_power_info: memory voltage where exposed, plus power and power limit
amdsmi_get_gpu_od_volt_info: V/F curve points and SCLK/MCLK ranges where supported; zero regions means unsupported
runtime_evidence_path.limitation: The API documentation says ECC enablement is independent of kernel support for error counters. RAS block status and RAS schema metadata do not themselves prove UMC GECC correction. Exact R9700 support and live state were not tested. AMD SMI 27.1.0 Python API docs mark ECC-state and RAS-block-status calls unsupported in VM guests. AMD SMI docs say guest VMs cannot retrieve ECC counts from host cards; ECC-state and per-block RAS-status Python calls are also unsupported in guests. Driver/library mismatch can make metric fields unavailable or N/A. These runtime APIs do not expose DRAM timing registers, and R9700 support was not queried.

runtime_controls_not_run: Current upstream Linux amdgpu_ras.c documents debugfs ras_ctrl operations to enable/disable RAS on supported blocks such as UMC, with state checked through ras/features. This is a driver RAS feature control, not a direct external-memory GECC switch; no write or injection was performed.

AMD SMI 27.1.0 C/C++ reference documents amdsmi_set_gpu_od_clk_info for SCLK/MCLK limits and amdsmi_set_gpu_od_volt_info for one of three voltage-curve points on bare-metal Linux; these are runtime controls, do not expose DRAM timing registers, and were not called. Exact R9700 support remains unverified.

local_evidence.artifact: AS04, AS07 and XFX software ROM
local_evidence.notes: ASUS/XFX bytes match; exact v3.1 definition absent in inspected public Linux ATOM header/parser; no count or mask decoded.
64 active CUs reported on XFX-subsystem functions only; no inference to ASUS.

areas.public_context: AMD specifies 64 CUs / 4096 stream processors. Current upstream GFX 12 code builds active CU topology from hardware register state and driver masks. Current upstream Linux amdgpu.disable_cu parsing adds a runtime user inactive mask; the GFX12 topology path combines user and hardware inactive state. This provides a software disable path only, not a way to restore hardware-inactive/fused resources, and exact ASUS/runtime dispatch is unknown.
areas.likely_control_layer: Silicon fuse/harvest state and runtime register topology, with driver reporting; not an established VBIOS gate.
areas.custom_vbios_relevance: No unlock field, no evidence of unused functional CUs, and no evidence a VBIOS could restore fused-off hardware.
areas.confidence: High that the table is opaque under available exact public definitions; low for ASUS-specific physical topology.
unknowns: GFX_INFO v3.1 definition
ASUS card identity and runtime CU bitmap
whether any disabled usable CU exists

local_evidence.notes: Public Linux names 0x00020000 as dynamic boot-config enable, XFX bit 0 as firmware posted, and 0x00000200 as SRAM ECC; 0x00004000 remains unknown. SRAM ECC bit is clear.
Current Linux header names this as two-stage BIST memory training capability; its absence is not evidence that all memory training is disabled.

local_evidence.artifact: Current upstream Linux AMDGPU RAS implementation snapshot
local_evidence.notes: When the software flag is present, the probe-time helper follows a special enable/disable path that sends PSP RAS TA commands. The source does not map this internal flag to ASUS ATOM firmware_capability bits or prove UMC GECC behavior on R9700.

areas.likely_control_layer: ATOM advertises dynamic boot configuration; PSP/driver GET/SET can manage GECC for a later boot. In a pinned upstream PSP RAS path, driver RAS support and module parameters can influence the persistent next-boot GECC choice.
areas.host_observation: XFX host reports GECC disabled; no boot option or PSP setting was changed. The host also logs hardware ability[101] ras_mask[101]. Current upstream emits these values with hexadecimal %x, and its RAS block enum maps bits 0 and 8 to UMC and DF; this is conditional because the exact custom-kernel source is not retained. It indicates driver RAS ability/mask only, not GECC enablement, error correction or counter values.
areas.custom_vbios_relevance: The dynamic boot-config bit is a capability, not an ECC enable bit. PSP runtime boot configuration is separate. Pinned upstream code shows ras_enable/ras_mask can indirectly affect the next-boot GECC selection when the dynamic-config path runs; this is not an immediate VBIOS ECC toggle or proof of correction. Do not change unnamed 0x4000 or infer correction from UMC capability metadata. Current upstream also has an internal RAS INIT_BY_VBIOS probe-time path that can send PSP RAS TA commands; this is a driver initialization branch, not evidence that ASUS ATOM bit 0x00004000 or any other inspected ROM bit controls it.
areas.confidence: High for raw capability bytes and upstream source behavior; low for exact ASUS/XFX runtime execution, the meaning of 0x4000, and active ECC correction.
unknowns: Meaning of 0x00004000
Why public product support is Linux-only
XFX live GECC behavior/counters
exact firmware-side feature enforcement

external_leads: A community R9700 report uses amdgpu.ras_enable=0 and reports GECC disabled. Upstream pinned PSP code documents a conditional next-boot GECC change when UMC RAS is unsupported, but the external log does not isolate that cause or measure correction. Treat as an unverified control-path observation, not an ECC switch recommendation.

A llama.cpp issue #28093 includes an external R9700 log: “GECC is disabled, set amdgpu_ras_enable=1 to enable GECC in next boot cycle if needed.” This supports the existence of a driver/PSP next-boot control message, but the issue concerns memory pressure during runtime suspend, does not identify a matching board, and does not measure ECC correction.

checked_sources.supports: Current amdgpu_smu.c maps MP1 IP 14.0.0/14.0.1/14.0.4/14.0.5 to smu_v14_0_0 and 14.0.2/14.0.3 to smu_v14_0_2. The external ROCm #9299 report logs 14.0.0; this does not identify the ASUS payload runtime path.

checked_sources.source: Current upstream Linux SMU 14.0.2 PowerPlay implementation
checked_sources.supports: Conditional PMFW combo-PowerPlay-table setup and feature-mask gating; generic OverDrive feature identifiers include GFX V/F curve, UCLK min/max and fan curve/minimum-PWM/acoustic/zero-RPM controls; generic memory-voltage identifiers include VMEMP_SCALING and VDDIO_MEM_SCALING. Driver interface expectation is 0x2e. None proves exact R9700/ASUS support or active values.

checked_sources.source: Current upstream Linux ATOM header and parser
checked_sources.type: primary upstream definition and implementation snapshots
checked_sources.supports: Names ENABLE_2STAGE_BIST_TRAINING=0x400 and defines GDDR6 vram_info timing/init structures for other table revisions. ASUS firmware capability leaves 0x400 clear and its vram_info pointer is null; those other table layouts are not applied.

checked_sources.source: Current upstream Linux PSP memory-training implementation
checked_sources.supports: Reads PSP runtime-database two-stage DRAM-training state and has cold-boot/resume training calls; generic code path only, exact ASUS/R9700 execution unknown.

checked_sources.source: Upstream Linux AMDGPU module-parameter documentation
checked_sources.supports: Documents forcelongtraining as forcing long memory training on resume; default zero selects short training. No parameter was changed and no resume experiment was run.

checked_sources.source: R9700 SMU interface and OverDrive reports, ROCm issues 6078 and 6101
checked_sources.type: secondary external contributor reports including AMD contributor comments
checked_sources.supports: External reports show firmware interface 0x32/0x33 versus driver 0x2e and differing fan/gpu_od outcomes. An Aug 2026 three-card report describes two ASUS cards with part 115-G287BP00-100 whose reported fan speed fell as junction temperature rose (about 2,350-2,520 RPM at 99-101 C versus about 3,500 RPM near 65 C; roughly 303 W sample), while runtime PM was held active; one card later had an SMU mailbox hang. The local payloads share the part label but the issue provides no ROM hash or AS04/AS07 revision. An AMD contributor says mismatch can be nonfatal and reports gpu_od on their R9700. These are not local measurements or proof of VBIOS causality.

checked_sources.source: Community R9700 SMU interface-version patch
checked_sources.supports: Proposes changing expected SMU 14.0.2 interface from 0x2e to 0x33 and reports R9700 fan/BACO/idle-power benefits; not upstream-validated and notes possible stale metrics.

checked_sources.source: R9700 s2idle SMU/DPM resume issue
checked_sources.type: secondary external contributor report with AMD contributor reproduction
checked_sources.supports: Two external R9700 samples report SMU/DPM resume failures; an AMD contributor reproduced an s2idle driver issue and said a patch was submitted. Issue remained open and the patch was not linked at the access date.

checked_sources.source: R9700 process-start throughput variance issue
checked_sources.supports: ROCm/TheRock #9228 (the same legacy issue #6347 after repository migration) reports process-spawn fast/slow decode states with similar SCLK; forcing high DPM did not prevent the transition, manual highest DPM reduced boost, and later comments report graph/attention configuration dependence. Runtime mechanism remains unresolved; no VBIOS attribution.

checked_sources.source: ROCm R9700 SMU mismatch issue #5908
checked_sources.supports: Reports SMU firmware interface 0x32 / PMFW 104.75 alongside a previous-command timeout and graphics ring timeout, with system input-lag and PCIe symptoms; correlation does not establish cause.

checked_sources.source: ROCm TheRock R9700 idle-power issue #9245
checked_sources.type: secondary external user report with comparative telemetry
checked_sources.supports: Reports 3-4% activity and about 18-19 W per R9700 using an idle HIP model versus 0% and 12-13 W for an equivalent Vulkan server; runtime/backend comparison, not a VBIOS result.

checked_sources.source: ASUS Turbo AS07 minimum-fan report
checked_sources.supports: A user reports an AS07 ROM lowering minimum fan speed from 30% to 12%; another says a full power cycle was required. The thread names a ROM but provides no measured raw log/hash or byte-to-field mapping.

checked_sources.source: Current upstream Linux AMDGPU thermal/fan sysfs documentation
checked_sources.supports: Documents runtime fan-curve and minimum-PWM controls, staged reads/writes and c commit semantics, plus PMFW-controlled automatic fan mode. Does not prove that the exact ASUS R9700 driver exposes these controls.

checked_sources.source: llama.cpp R9700 GECC next-boot log, issue #28093
checked_sources.supports: Includes an R9700 driver log saying GECC is disabled and amdgpu_ras_enable=1 can enable GECC in the next boot cycle. This supports the existence of a driver/PSP next-boot message, not correction or exact board identity.

checked_sources.source: AMD SMI Python API docs 27.1.0
checked_sources.supports: Read-only ECC mask/status/count and RAS status/schema APIs; read-only power, voltage and clock metrics; supported clock levels/current index; memory overdrive percent; and voltage-frequency curve points/ranges when supported. Several APIs are unsupported in VM guests. The docs distinguish API/device support from actual measurements; exact R9700 support was not exercised.

checked_sources.source: R9700 SMU/MES host-freeze issue #9299
checked_sources.supports: Two external dual-R9700 setups report SMU/MES queue failures and total host hangs. The first reports PMFW 104.79/interface 0x33 and MP1 IP 14.0.0 with 230 W cap and normal temperatures; its author correlates events with bursty clock/power plus SDMA/PCIe traffic. A second contributor reports a similar failure with another R9700 firmware string. External reports do not establish VBIOS causality or a local ASUS field.

checked_sources.source: Current upstream Linux AMDGPU RAS debugfs control implementation
checked_sources.supports: Documents per-block ras_ctrl enable/disable and error-injection operations, supported-block checks, and ras/features status confirmation. This is a driver-side RAS feature control, not proof of UMC GECC or memory correction; no control or injection was performed.

checked_sources.source: Current upstream Linux SMU 14.0.0 PowerPlay implementation and interface header
checked_sources.type: primary upstream implementation and definition snapshots
checked_sources.supports: Current generic MP1 14.0.0 branch is distinct from 14.0.2, is marked APU-oriented, uses driver interface 0x7 (versus 0x2e for 14.0.2), and returns zero for VDDGFX/VDDSOC sensor cases. An external R9700 issue reports MP1 14.0.0 with PMFW interface 0x33; the exact driver/firmware pairing and R9700 applicability are unknown.

checked_sources.source: AMD SMI 27.2.0 install and CLI documentation plus 27.1.0 changelog
checked_sources.supports: AMD SMI retrieves metrics through amdgpu; driver/library version mismatches can make fields unavailable or N/A, including when GPU metrics layouts are unsupported. Guest VMs cannot retrieve ECC counts from host cards; amd-smi static --ras can show enabled/disabled host RAS feature state. This is a telemetry-availability constraint, not evidence of GECC correction.

checked_sources.source: Current upstream Linux exact-revision UMC v4.0 parser
checked_sources.supports: amdgpu_atomfirmware_get_umc_info() accepts frev 4/crev 0, reads v40.channel_num and v40.channel_width, and computes width as channel_num * (1 << channel_width), yielding 256 bits for the ASUS values 16 and 4. The related amdgpu_atomfirmware_mem_ecc_supported() parser treats ENABLE_ECC_CAPABLE as capability and separately derives ras_default_ecc_enabled from DEFAULT_MEM_ECC_ENABLE. This is code interpretation, not a physical measurement or proof of active correction.

checked_sources.source: AMD SMI C/C++ API docs 27.1.0 — clock and voltage setters
checked_sources.supports: Documents amdsmi_set_gpu_od_clk_info for SCLK/MCLK min/max ranges and amdsmi_set_gpu_od_volt_info for V/F curve points on bare-metal Linux; VM guests are unsupported. These are runtime controls, not DRAM timing table access or a demonstrated persistent VBIOS edit. Exact R9700 support was not exercised.

checked_sources.source: Current upstream Linux AMDGPU RAS boot initialization and flag definition
checked_sources.type: primary upstream implementation and definition snapshots
checked_sources.supports: The internal AMDGPU_RAS_FLAG_INIT_BY_VBIOS software flag selects a probe-time RAS feature enable/disable path that sends PSP RAS TA commands. It is not mapped here to ASUS ATOM firmware_capability bits and does not prove UMC GECC state or correction.

targeted_four_area_research.practical_conclusion: No evidence-backed edit target is established in these four areas. Runtime tools offer optional, version- and device-dependent clock/voltage control and read-only telemetry; these are useful characterization paths, not proof of a persistent ROM edit target. Exact-board association, active PowerPlay/SMU source, memory configuration, silicon topology and ECC state remain necessary evidence.
